claims.text: The initial and baseline material is unchanged bulk HfNbTaTiZr.
Oxygen vacancies can be introduced into bulk HfNbTaTiZr as the proposed intervention.
Introducing oxygen vacancies into HfNbTaTiZr produces lattice distortion and strain fluctuations.
Lattice distortion and strain fluctuations strengthen phonon scattering.
Stronger phonon scattering associated with lattice distortion and strain fluctuations reduces lattice thermal conductivity.
Oxygen-vacancy-containing bulk HfNbTaTiZr will have lower lattice thermal conductivity than unchanged bulk HfNbTaTiZr.
The predicted reduction applies from 0 to 200 K in the bulk material state.
The magnitude of the predicted reduction is uncertain and requires experimental verification.
The hypothesis can be tested by comparing samples with and without oxygen vacancies using thermal-conductivity, lattice-parameter, and electrical-resistivity measurements.
Failure to observe a reduction in lattice thermal conductivity after the intervention would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The starting material is specified only as HfNbTaTiZr, with no oxygen-bearing phase or initial oxygen occupancy, yet the intervention is creation of oxygen vacancies. An oxygen vacancy requires oxygen to be present initially at defined sites, so the intervention is ill-defined for the stated unchanged baseline.
